name: Runner Extras - Object System Table
brief: Issue #3071: Object (2000000001) is the legacy application-database object registry, and a real service tier holds NO rows in it. The runner used to project its own object inventory there (#2774); that projection is removed. This suite pins the three things that are about the RUNNER rather than about BC: that the emptiness is a per-table policy and not a missing inventory, that an empty table still ANSWERS on all four DataAccess request paths, and that the four OemText columns stay readable.
description: WHAT THIS TABLE HOLDS IS PLAIN BC BEHAVIOUR AND IS ASSERTED UPSTREAM, NOT HERE. Corpus codeunit 61202 (tests/al-language-onprem/record/TestObjectSystemTable.al, corpus PR StefanMaron/BusinessCentral.AL.Language.Tests#197, merged as c04b236) reads 2000000001 from a Target = OnPrem app and asserts it is present, readable and EMPTY; it passed on the BC OnPrem legs 27.0, 27.3, 28.0, 28.1, 28.2, 28.3 and 28.4, and its centerpiece carries a control arm reading the populated sibling Object Metadata in the same session so that 'empty' cannot be an unreadable table misreported. The eighth OnPrem leg, 27.5, failed its app publish (HTTP 401/422) and executed nothing, so it is not a dissent. Repeating that claim down here would make it the runner agreeing with itself, which is how the two stale assertions #3066 found survived. So this suite asserts only what is runner-specific. First, the POLICY: the runner still projects AllObj (2000000038) from the same EnumerateKnownAlObjects inventory Object's rows used to come from, so Object being empty WHILE AllObj lists these very objects, in one session, distinguishes 'this table is deliberately not synthesised' from 'this run has no object inventory' - and is the arm that fails if the projection is ever reinstated. Second, that an empty table still ANSWERS rather than refusing, on all four DataAccess request paths - keyed Get, find, count, and IsEmpty, which RecordImplementation.IsEmptyAsync serves from its own ExistsAsync rather than from CountAsync - with the same four paths on AllObj as the control; refusing at row-build time takes out all four at once, which is the #2519 trap. Third, that fields 2, 4, 12 and 50 stay readable: Microsoft's AL compiler treats those four Text[n] columns as OemText (CodeGenerator.IsOemTextFieldOnObjectTable) and the runner mirrors it when building the metatable; get it wrong and the read throws NavObjectDefinitionChangedException rather than returning a wrong value. With the row projection gone that predicate has no rows left to protect, so this is the only test that would notice it being deleted as dead. Target is OnPrem, not Cloud: Microsoft declares this table Scope = OnPrem, so a Cloud-target app fails AL0296 on `Record "Object"`; AlRunner.Tests/RecordRefCompilationTargetScopeTests runs BC's own CheckIsOpenAllowed against 2000000001 in both target directions.
